title: How to Make a Difference: Part 1

sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: You can take a horse to water, but you can't make him drink.
sentences.zh: 你可以把马牵到水边，但你无法强迫它喝水。

sentences.en: It's an old saying, but it captures a fundamental truth about human nature.
sentences.zh: 这是一句古老的谚语，但它揭示了人性中一个基本的真理。

sentences.en: How often have you come by people who fail to seize the opportunities in front of them,
sentences.zh: 你遇到过多少次这样的人，他们无法抓住眼前的机会，

sentences.en: who decline to make the most of the privileges they've been given?
sentences.zh: 拒绝充分利用他们所拥有的特权？

sentences.en: If you're a parent or a teacher, you may have sometimes felt like saying to a kid,
sentences.zh: 如果你是家长或老师，你可能有时会想对孩子说：

sentences.en: I can't make you want it.
If you're a manager, perhaps you've told an employee,
sentences.zh: 如果你是管理者，也许你曾告诉员工：

sentences.en: there's a ladder over here, but you have to be the one to climb it.
sentences.zh: 梯子就在这里，但你必须自己去爬。

sentences.en: Sometimes the thing that needs to be seized is not an opportunity, but a lifeline.
sentences.zh: 有时，人们需要抓住的不是机会，而是一根救命稻草。

sentences.en: Do you know people stuck in bad situations, unhappy marriages, dead-end jobs,
sentences.zh: 你是否认识一些身陷困境的人，比如不幸的婚姻、毫无前途的工作、

sentences.en: soul-crushing living conditions, who seem unwilling to escape even when the chance presents itself?
sentences.zh: 令人窒息的生活环境，即使机会摆在面前，他们似乎也不愿逃离？

sentences.en: Today on the show, and in a follow-up episode next week,
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，以及下周的后续剧集中，

sentences.en: why do some people act on the possibilities before them,
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨为什么有些人会采取行动去把握眼前的可能性，

sentences.en: while others believe that nothing they do can make a difference?
sentences.zh: 而另一些人却认为无论做什么都无济于事？

sentences.en: How to discover, or rediscover, your ability to change things for the better?
sentences.zh: 如何发现或重新发现你改变现状的能力？
本周，请关注《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Every day, life presents us with small moments of possibility.
sentences.zh: 每一天，生活都会为我们呈现出微小的可能性时刻。

sentences.en: A conversation that could change the course of a career.
sentences.zh: 一次可能改变职业生涯走向的谈话。

sentences.en: A relationship that could be repaired.
A job posting that could become the start of something new.
sentences.zh: 一份可能成为新起点的工作招聘启事。

sentences.en: Some people step toward those moments almost instinctively.
sentences.zh: 有些人几乎是本能地迈向这些时刻。

sentences.en: Others turn away without even trying.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人甚至不去尝试就转身离开。

sentences.en: Today, we explore the hidden psychological forces that determine which path we take,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探索决定我们选择哪条道路的隐藏心理力量，

sentences.en: and why the stories we tell about ourselves can become self-fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么我们对自己讲述的故事会成为自我实现的预言。

sentences.en: psychologist Martin Seligman has spent many years studying these questions.
sentences.zh: 心理学家马丁·塞利格曼多年来一直致力于研究这些问题。

sentences.en: Marty Seligman, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 马蒂·塞利格曼，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Marty, I want to take you back to what might be your earliest memory.
sentences.zh: 马蒂，我想带你回到你最早的记忆中。

sentences.en: Tell me the story about a time when you saw your mother crying.
sentences.zh: 给我讲讲你看到母亲哭泣的那次经历。

sentences.en: I'm two and a half years old, and I think this really is my first memory.
sentences.zh: 那时我两岁半，我想这确实是我最早的记忆。

sentences.en: And I hear these heartbroken sobs and gasps coming from the next room.
sentences.zh: 我听到隔壁房间传来心碎的啜泣声和喘息声。

sentences.en: And I run in to see my mother, and there she is sitting on the second step of the stairs to the upstairs
sentences.zh: 我跑进去看我的母亲，她正坐在通往楼上的楼梯的第二级台阶上，

sentences.en: with her head in her hands, and she's sobbing.
Many years later, I tried to figure out what was really going on.
sentences.zh: 多年以后，我试图弄清楚当时到底发生了什么。
那应该是在1945年的早中期。

sentences.en: I think the concentration camps had opened,
sentences.zh: 我想集中营已经开放了，

sentences.en: and all of my mother's Hungarian relatives,
sentences.zh: 我母亲所有的匈牙利亲戚，

sentences.en: her family that she abandoned in Hungary, were murdered.
sentences.zh: 她留在匈牙利并抛弃的家人，都被谋杀了。

sentences.en: But something happened to me then, Shankar, that actually fits with the hidden brain.
sentences.zh: 但那时发生在我身上的一件事，尚卡尔，实际上与“隐藏的大脑”相吻合。

sentences.en: And that is when I look at the photos of me,
sentences.zh: 那就是当我看着自己的照片时，

sentences.en: I'm a smiley, hair down to my shoulders,
sentences.zh: 在三岁左右之前，我是一个爱笑、头发垂到肩膀的，

sentences.en: ebullient kid up until about age three.
And then, when I look at my photos up to my teenage and beyond,
sentences.zh: 然后，当我看着我青少年时期及以后的照片时，

sentences.en: I'm tight-lipped, I'm unsmiling, I'm looking thoughtful.
sentences.zh: 我紧闭双唇，不再微笑，神情若有所思。

sentences.en: And when I look at my really early photographs of this smiley, ebullient kid,
sentences.zh: 当我看着那些非常早期的照片，看着那个爱笑、充满活力的孩子时，

sentences.en: Marty, I want to skip forward to another experience a few years later when you were 13.
sentences.zh: 马蒂，我想跳到几年后你13岁时的另一段经历。

sentences.en: Your dad was driving you in the car, and he shared something with you that was very disturbing.
sentences.zh: 你父亲开车送你时，和你分享了一件非常令人不安的事情。
描述一下当时发生了什么。

sentences.en: I'm 13 years old, and I go to my second day of playing golf with my friend Bob Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 我13岁，正要去和朋友鲍勃·凯泽打第二天的高尔夫球。

sentences.en: And when my father drops us off at the golf course, he says,
sentences.zh: 当我父亲把我们送到高尔夫球场时，他说：

sentences.en: I can't feel my left arm.
I slept overnight at my best friend Jeff Albert's house,
sentences.zh: 我在最好的朋友杰夫·阿尔伯特家过夜，

sentences.en: and I had this dreadful feeling that something was wrong.
sentences.zh: 我有一种可怕的感觉，觉得出事了。

sentences.en: And I walked home probably nine in the morning the next day,
sentences.zh: 第二天早上九点左右，我走回家，

sentences.en: and there was my father being dragged out on a stretcher into an ambulance.
sentences.zh: 看到我父亲正被抬上担架，送进救护车。

sentences.en: And he had had a small stroke.
And then within a couple of days, Shankar, my mother said my father had had massive strokes.
sentences.zh: 几天之内，尚卡尔，我母亲说我父亲中风很严重。

sentences.en: And in the next couple of months, I visited my father reluctantly.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几个月里，我不情愿地去探望父亲。

sentences.en: I was really afraid of this helplessness that I saw.
sentences.zh: 我真的很害怕看到那种无助感。

sentences.en: And he basically said, I'm helpless.
I love you and your sister and your mother, and I don't want to die.
sentences.zh: 我爱你，爱你姐姐和你母亲，我不想死。

sentences.en: And I think this was the major experience of my childhood.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我童年时期最重大的经历。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, Marty, if you can spend a minute talking about the helplessness that you had seen in your mother when she was crying,
sentences.zh: 马蒂，我想请你花点时间谈谈你在母亲哭泣时看到的无助，

sentences.en: the helplessness that you saw in your father when he told you that he was afraid of dying.
sentences.zh: 以及你在父亲告诉你他害怕死亡时看到的无助。

sentences.en: How did that make you feel?
It's hard for me to remember, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我很难回忆起来。

sentences.en: I know my response was avoidance, not to visit my father, not to see more of it.
sentences.zh: 我知道我的反应是逃避，不去探望父亲，不去面对更多这样的场景。

sentences.en: But very interestingly, when I got to college, I found myself wearing black all the time and thinking all the time about death.
sentences.zh: 但非常有趣的是，当我上大学时，我发现自己总是穿着黑色的衣服，满脑子想的都是死亡。

sentences.en: I think those were the, if you will, the hidden brain consequences of whatever happened when I visited my father.
sentences.zh: 我想那些就是，如果你愿意这么说的话，我探望父亲时所发生的一切在“隐藏的大脑”层面留下的后果。

sentences.en: Our experiences teach us lessons about the world.
sentences.zh: 我们的经历教会我们关于世界的道理。

sentences.en: They also teach us lessons about ourselves, whether it's worth taking a risk, whether setbacks are temporary,
sentences.zh: 它们也教会我们关于自己的道理，比如是否值得冒险，挫折是否是暂时的，

sentences.en: and whether our actions can shape what happens next.
sentences.zh: 以及我们的行为是否能塑造接下来的发展。

sentences.en: Those lessons can be remarkably powerful.
sentences.zh: 这些教训可能具有惊人的力量。

sentences.en: When we come back, Marty steps into a psych lab and starts to understand the true horror of helplessness.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，马蒂将走进心理实验室，开始了解无助感的真正恐怖之处。
你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: All of us carry around a private explanation for why things happen.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都随身带着一套私人的解释系统，用来解释事情发生的原因。

sentences.en: When something goes wrong, we ask ourselves, was this just bad luck?
sentences.zh: 当事情出错时，我们会问自己，这只是运气不好吗？
这种情况会持续下去吗？

sentences.en: Does it say something about who I am?
sentences.zh: 这是否说明了我是一个什么样的人？

sentences.en: We usually don't notice ourselves asking these questions, but the answers can quietly shape the course of our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们通常不会注意到自己在问这些问题，但答案却在悄无声息地塑造我们的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: Martin Seligman is a psychologist at the University of Pennsylvania who studies the science of human flourishing.
sentences.zh: 马丁·塞利格曼是宾夕法尼亚大学的心理学家，研究人类繁荣的科学。

sentences.en: Marty, you told me about some personal encounters with hopelessness and helplessness that you had as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 马蒂，你告诉过我你青少年时期经历的一些关于绝望和无助的个人遭遇。

sentences.en: A few years later, as a 21-year-old entering graduate school in psychology, you had the opportunity to explore these same themes in a research context.
sentences.zh: 几年后，作为一名21岁进入心理学研究生院的学生，你有机会在研究背景下探索同样的主题。

sentences.en: Paint a picture for me of what you saw when you first entered the psychologist Richard Solomon's lab.
sentences.zh: 请为我描绘一下你第一次走进心理学家理查德·所罗门的实验室时所看到的景象。

sentences.en: What was he working on, and what did you see?
sentences.zh: 他在研究什么，你看到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, they were doing experiments that I actually felt were horrifying.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们正在进行的实验，我实际上觉得非常可怕。

sentences.en: I'm a dog lover, and psychologists were working with dogs at the time and giving them mild to moderate electric shock.
sentences.zh: 我是一个爱狗人士，当时心理学家正在用狗做实验，并给它们施加轻度到中度的电击。

sentences.en: So these were very difficult experiments for me to participate in, but there was something very puzzling going on,
sentences.zh: 所以这些实验对我来说非常难以参与，但当时发生了一些非常令人困惑的事情，

sentences.en: and that is the primary puzzle that animal learning psychologists were working on was Pavlovian conditioning.
sentences.zh: 那就是动物学习心理学家们正在研究的主要难题是巴甫洛夫条件反射。

sentences.en: A dog or a rat or a person gets a tone followed by a shock, and then the tone comes to elicit fear.
sentences.zh: 狗、老鼠或人听到一种声音后会受到电击，然后这种声音就会引发恐惧。

sentences.en: And they were working on that, and indeed, in phase one of their experiments, dogs were put into a hammock and given Pavlovian conditioning with shock.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正在研究这个，事实上，在他们实验的第一阶段，狗被放在吊床上，并接受了巴甫洛夫式的电击条件反射训练。

sentences.en: But they were running into this enormous problem, is they wanted to see the next day, when dogs were put in a different situation,
sentences.zh: 但他们遇到了一个巨大的问题，因为他们想看看第二天，当狗被放在不同的环境中时，

sentences.en: a shuttle box in which the dogs just needed to run from one side to the other to turn off shock, that the dogs didn't run.
sentences.zh: 一个穿梭箱，狗只需要从一边跑到另一边就能关掉电击，结果狗却没有跑。

sentences.en: So in some ways, what you observed was that on day one, the dogs were essentially learning to associate the painful electric shock with the stone,
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，你观察到的是，在第一天，狗基本上学会了将痛苦的电击与声音联系起来，

sentences.en: but they could do nothing about it.
On day two, the dogs were placed in a position where they were hearing these stones, and they could escape, but in fact, they were not doing so.
sentences.zh: 第二天，狗被放在一个可以听到这些声音并可以逃脱的位置，但实际上，它们并没有这样做。

sentences.en: And this was a puzzle for the people in your lab.
sentences.zh: 这对你实验室里的人来说是一个谜。

sentences.en: You interpreted this in some ways as the dogs experiencing helplessness?
sentences.zh: 你是否在某种程度上将其解释为狗体验到了无助感？

sentences.en: I said, you know, there's something much more important in Pavlovian conditioning than learning the association of a tone with shock.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道，在巴甫洛夫条件反射中，比学习声音与电击的关联更重要的事情是，

sentences.en: In Pavlovian conditioning, by definition, there's nothing you can do about it.
sentences.zh: 在巴甫洛夫条件反射中，根据定义，你对此无能为力。

sentences.en: The shock comes regardless of what you do.
sentences.zh: 无论你做什么，电击都会发生。

sentences.en: And their interest was, did you learn to be afraid of the tone?
sentences.zh: 他们的兴趣在于，你是否学会了害怕那种声音？

sentences.en: But could it be that more important to an animal or person is the fact that you're helpless in this situation, and that you might be learning that nothing you do matters?
sentences.zh: 但有没有可能，对动物或人来说更重要的是，你在这种情况下感到无助，并且你可能正在学习到无论你做什么都无济于事？

sentences.en: And if that were so, it would make sense that the next day, when you got shock again, you just lay there and didn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，那么第二天当你再次受到电击时，你只是躺在那里什么都不做，这就说得通了。

sentences.en: So this began a major uphill battle between me and the behaviorists, and what was behind it was the notion that people and animals were cognitive, that they could think,
sentences.zh: 于是，我和行为主义者之间开始了一场重大的艰苦斗争，其背后的理念是，人和动物是有认知能力的，他们可以思考，

sentences.en: that they could integrate experience across time.
sentences.zh: 他们可以整合跨时间的经验。

sentences.en: And we theorize that the animals has learned that nothing they did mattered.
sentences.zh: 我们推测，动物已经学会了无论它们做什么都无济于事。

sentences.en: I understand that a psychologist named Donald Hiroto extended some of this work with a very interesting experiment involving human beings.
sentences.zh: 我了解到一位名叫唐纳德·希罗托的心理学家通过一个涉及人类的非常有趣的实验扩展了这项工作。

sentences.en: Describe for me what Hiroto did, Marty.
sentences.zh: 马蒂，请描述一下希罗托做了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Don Hiroto said, let's try exactly the same thing with humans.
sentences.zh: 是的，唐·希罗托说，让我们在人类身上尝试完全相同的事情。

sentences.en: So what Don did, and it became an entire field, he put, for day one, headphones on people and turned on a loud, annoying noise.
sentences.zh: 所以唐所做的，后来成为了一个完整的领域，他在第一天给人们戴上耳机，并打开一种响亮、恼人的噪音。

sentences.en: Now, this is the equivalent of shock, nothing traumatic, but very annoying.
sentences.zh: 这相当于电击，没有什么创伤性，但非常恼人。

sentences.en: And for one group, nothing you did mattered.
sentences.zh: 对于一组人来说，无论你做什么都无济于事。

sentences.en: For a second group, you got the tone, but you could press a button to turn off the noise.
sentences.zh: 对于第二组人，你听到了声音，但你可以按一个按钮来关掉噪音。

sentences.en: And then the next day, Don built a human shuttle box, about four feet long.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天，唐建造了一个人类穿梭箱，大约四英尺长。

sentences.en: You put your hand on one side, and noise went on.
sentences.zh: 你把手放在一边，噪音就会响起。

sentences.en: And all you had to do was move your hand to the other side of the shuttle box.
sentences.zh: 你所要做的就是把手移到穿梭箱的另一边。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, he found that the people who had had the helplessness experience, inescapable noise, just sat there with their hand in the shuttle box and didn't move.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，那些有过无助体验、经历过无法逃避的噪音的人，只是坐在那里，把手放在穿梭箱里，一动不动。

sentences.en: And that was the beginning of a vibrant field of learned helplessness, which went way beyond the animal laboratory to the question of human trauma and human depression.
sentences.zh: 这就是“习得性无助”这一充满活力的领域的开端，它远远超出了动物实验室，延伸到了人类创伤和人类抑郁的问题上。

sentences.en: So you used this term learned helplessness a moment ago, and it's an important term to stop and ponder for a second.
sentences.zh: 刚才你用了“习得性无助”这个词，这是一个值得停下来思考一下的重要术语。

sentences.en: How would you describe the phenomenon of learned helplessness, Marty?
sentences.zh: 马蒂，你会如何描述习得性无助这种现象？

sentences.en: Here are the basics of learned helplessness.
sentences.zh: 以下是习得性无助的基本要素。
首先，事件是无法逃避的。
无论你做什么都无济于事。

sentences.en: And what we believed was that people learned that nothing they did mattered.
sentences.zh: 我们认为人们学会了无论他们做什么都无济于事。

sentences.en: The first consequence is you became passive later on,
sentences.zh: 第一个后果是你后来变得被动，

sentences.en: particularly when you faced a similar kind of annoying or traumatic event.
sentences.zh: 特别是在你面临类似恼人或创伤性事件时。

sentences.en: And the second problem was that you had a lot of trouble learning that you could do something about it.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是，你很难学会你可以采取行动来改变现状。

sentences.en: So once you had learned that nothing you did mattered, it was very hard to unlearn it.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你学会了无论做什么都无济于事，就很难再摆脱这种想法。

sentences.en: But the most surprising thing we found, Shankar, was there was an emotional consequence as well, that people felt sad and anxious.
sentences.zh: 但尚卡尔，我们发现最令人惊讶的是，它还有情感上的后果，人们会感到悲伤和焦虑。

sentences.en: So there was passivity, cognitive difficulty, and emotional sadness and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所以当时出现了被动、认知困难，以及情绪上的悲伤和焦虑。

sentences.en: Importantly, this was not the result of trauma itself, we controlled for that, it was a result of not having any control over trauma.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，这并非创伤本身的结果——我们对此进行了控制变量——而是因为对创伤毫无掌控感所导致的结果。

sentences.en: And so that was the operative variable that in many ways has been the arc of my entire life's work.
sentences.zh: 这正是那个核心变量，在许多方面，它构成了我毕生研究的主线。

sentences.en: And of course, you can think about so many groups of people who experience something like this in the real world.
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以想到现实世界中许多经历过类似情况的人群。

sentences.en: If you're a small child, for instance, your life is governed by people who are bigger than you, more powerful than you.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你是一个小孩，你的生活是由那些比你高大、比你更有权力的人所支配的。

sentences.en: And if they treat you badly, you might not have options to escape your circumstances.
sentences.zh: 如果他们虐待你，你可能没有选择去逃离自己的处境。

sentences.en: If you're trapped in poverty, for example, you might not have the ability to escape your circumstances.
sentences.zh: 如果你深陷贫困，例如，你可能没有能力逃离自己的处境。

sentences.en: And you can quickly see how these experiments in the lab might have much, much bigger consequences in the real world.
sentences.zh: 你可以很快看出，这些实验室里的实验在现实世界中可能会产生多么巨大的后果。

sentences.en: And so I thought a great deal about poverty, about war, and in particular, adult circumstances in which you're helpless.
sentences.zh: 所以我对贫困、战争，特别是成年人在无助状态下的处境进行了大量的思考。

sentences.en: And there was a literature that I got very interested in about sudden death itself.
sentences.zh: 当时有一篇关于猝死本身的文献让我非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: I remember interviewing someone named Harold Kushner, who had just come back from being a prisoner of war in Hanoi.
sentences.zh: 我记得曾采访过一位名叫哈罗德·库什纳的人，他刚从河内的战俘营回来。

sentences.en: And Harold told me the story of his best friend, Robert.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德向我讲述了他最好的朋友罗伯特的故事。

sentences.en: They were down to about 95 pounds by then.
sentences.zh: 那时他们的体重已经降到了大约95磅。

sentences.en: But they kept Robert going by telling them that he was first on the list to be released,
sentences.zh: 但他们一直鼓励罗伯特，告诉他他是名单上第一个被释放的人，

sentences.en: and that in December he was going to be released, particularly if he cooperated and told them about what he did during the war.
sentences.zh: 而且如果他配合并交代他在战争期间的所作所为，他就能在十二月获释。

sentences.en: Well, December first came around and he wasn't released.
sentences.zh: 结果十二月一号到了，他并没有被释放。

sentences.en: And Harold told me, Robert just shriveled up and within a few days was dead.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德告诉我，罗伯特整个人一下子就垮了，没过几天就去世了。

sentences.en: So I was not only interested in early experiences of abuse, helplessness, systematic experiences like poverty,
sentences.zh: 所以我不仅对早期的虐待、无助感以及像贫困这样的系统性经历感兴趣，

sentences.en: but adult experiences in which even though you've had a lifetime of doing well and you're deprived of control,
sentences.zh: 还对成年后的经历感兴趣，即即便你一生都过得很好，但当你被剥夺了掌控权时，

sentences.en: I understand that at one point, Marty, you spotted a connection between what you were seeing with learned helplessness
sentences.zh: 马蒂，我了解到在某个阶段，你发现了你在习得性无助中观察到的现象与抑郁症这一普遍现象之间的联系。

sentences.en: and the pervasive phenomenon of depression.
sentences.zh: 谈谈你所建立的这种联系吧。

sentences.en: Talk about that connection that you made.
sentences.zh: 谈谈你所建立的这种联系吧。

sentences.en: When I was a graduate student, one of my young professors was someone named Jim Geer.
sentences.zh: 当我还是研究生时，我的一位年轻教授叫吉姆·吉尔。

sentences.en: And Jim came up to look at the helpless dogs.
sentences.zh: 吉姆过来观察那些无助的狗。

sentences.en: And he looked at them and he said, Marty, that's depression.
sentences.zh: 他看着它们说：马蒂，那就是抑郁症。

sentences.en: I said, well, what's depression, Jim?
sentences.zh: 我说：好吧，吉姆，什么是抑郁症？

sentences.en: And now, if we go back to 1970, depression was not a category.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果我们回到1970年，抑郁症还不是一个分类。

sentences.en: So if you looked at the diagnostic categories, there was something called manic depression.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你查看当时的诊断分类，只有一种叫躁郁症的东西。

sentences.en: But by 1975, the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of the American Psychiatric Association
sentences.zh: 但到了1975年，美国精神医学学会的《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》

sentences.en: for the first time isolated a new disorder called unipolar depression.
sentences.zh: 第一次分离出了一种新的疾病，称为单相抑郁症。

sentences.en: Unipolar depression had nine different symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 单相抑郁症有九种不同的症状。

sentences.en: And if five of them were present for two weeks or more, you got the diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 如果其中五种症状持续两周或以上，你就会被确诊。

sentences.en: So the symptoms were passivity, cognitive difficulty, sadness, anxiety, trouble sleeping,
sentences.zh: 这些症状包括被动、认知困难、悲伤、焦虑、睡眠障碍、

sentences.en: food not tasting good, numbness, lack of mirth, and thoughts of death.
sentences.zh: 食之无味、麻木、缺乏快乐感以及死亡念头。

sentences.en: So, I looked at those nine symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 于是，我研究了那九种症状。

sentences.en: And then I looked at the very large literature on learned helplessness, which had accumulated by 1975.
sentences.zh: 然后我查阅了到1975年为止积累的关于习得性无助的大量文献。

sentences.en: Eight of the nine symptoms were present.
sentences.zh: 九种症状中有八种都出现了。

sentences.en: The only one that wasn't present in the laboratory was thought to death.
sentences.zh: 唯一没有在实验室中出现的就是死亡念头。

sentences.en: And that's probably because we were using things like loud noise.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为我们当时使用的是像巨大噪音之类的刺激。

sentences.en: And so, I proposed that learned helplessness was a model of depression.
sentences.zh: 因此，我提出习得性无助是抑郁症的一种模型。

sentences.en: And indeed, that went on to become the leading model of depression.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它后来确实成为了抑郁症的主导模型。

sentences.en: And it led to a vibrant neuroscience in which people tried out drugs that broke up helplessness in the laboratory in rats, for example, and then tried them in people.
sentences.zh: 它带动了活跃的神经科学研究，人们尝试用药物来打破实验室大鼠的无助感，然后再在人类身上进行试验。

sentences.en: And it turned out the drugs that worked to break up helplessness in the laboratory became the leading antidepressants.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，那些在实验室中能打破无助感的药物，成为了主要抗抑郁药。

sentences.en: Now, the research that you were conducting at this time was focused on the people who experienced adverse conditions.
sentences.zh: 那么，你当时进行的研究主要集中在那些经历过逆境的人身上。

sentences.en: They became helpless and then perhaps even depressed.
sentences.zh: 他们变得无助，甚至可能变得抑郁。

sentences.en: But there was also another group of subjects that, at first, you didn't pay so much attention to.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一组受试者，起初你并没有给予太多关注。

sentences.en: Tell me about this group of subjects, Marty.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说这组受试者吧，马蒂。

sentences.en: Who were they and what did you notice?
sentences.zh: 他们是谁？你注意到了什么？

sentences.en: In the entire helplessness literature, both in animals and people, the helplessness effect was statistical.
sentences.zh: 在整个无助感文献中，无论是动物还是人类，无助感效应都是统计学上的。

sentences.en: So, when I described a person becoming passive and just sitting in the shuttle box and not doing anything, that was five out of eight people on average.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我描述一个人变得被动，只是坐在穿梭箱里什么都不做时，平均八个人里有五个是这样。

sentences.en: Or a helpless rat, that five out of eight of them were helpless.
sentences.zh: 或者一只无助的老鼠，八只里有五只是无助的。

sentences.en: But about a third were not.
sentences.zh: 但大约有三分之一不是这样。

sentences.en: And so, starting in the 1970s, I began to ask, well, what is it about some people, some animals, that made them resilient or resistant to helplessness?
sentences.zh: 因此，从20世纪70年代开始，我开始思考：是什么让一些人、一些动物具有韧性或对无助感产生抵抗力？

sentences.en: What is it about some people that make you, in spite of the fact that your girlfriend has rejected you, your stocks have gone down?
sentences.zh: 是什么让一些人在女朋友拒绝你、股票下跌的情况下，依然能坚持下去？

sentences.en: What is it that gives some people the courage to transcend helplessness?
sentences.zh: 是什么赋予了一些人超越无助感的勇气？

sentences.en: And this was the turning point in my career.
sentences.zh: 这是我职业生涯的转折点。

sentences.en: So, you started thinking about what might distinguish the people who become helpless and passive in the face of adversity from those who remain motivated and energetic.
sentences.zh: 所以，你开始思考是什么区分了那些在逆境面前变得无助和被动的人，以及那些依然保持动力和活力的人。

sentences.en: Were there differences between the groups in the stories they told about their experiences, Marty?
sentences.zh: 马蒂，这些群体在讲述各自经历时，是否存在差异？

sentences.en: Yes, and it led to nailing down what it was about the one-third of people who didn't become helpless.
sentences.zh: 是的，这最终确定了那三分之一没有变得无助的人的特质。

sentences.en: These were vague terms to me at the time.
sentences.zh: 在当时，这些对我来说还是模糊的术语。

sentences.en: But what we wondered was, when you have a bad experience, a traumatic experience, you could believe, there's nothing I can do and I'm helpless.
sentences.zh: 但我们想知道的是，当你经历了一次糟糕的、创伤性的体验时，你可能会认为：我无能为力，我感到无助。

sentences.en: But we postulated from the stories we heard that what protected people from helplessness, what made them resilient,
sentences.zh: 但根据我们听到的故事，我们推测，保护人们免受无助感困扰、使他们具有韧性的，

sentences.en: was different dimensions of interpreting what happens to you when bad events occur.
sentences.zh: 是人们在坏事发生时对事件解读的不同维度。

sentences.en: So, first, you might believe that the bad event was going to last forever.
sentences.zh: 首先，你可能会认为坏事会永远持续下去。

sentences.en: Or, you might believe it was temporary.
sentences.zh: 或者，你可能会认为它是暂时的。

sentences.en: And so, for example, if you fail an examination, you might say, I had a hangover.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果你考试不及格，你可能会说：我当时宿醉了。

sentences.en: That means the next time you confront an examination, you'll be fine.
sentences.zh: 这意味着下次面对考试时，你会表现得很好。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you might say to yourself, I'm stupid.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你可能会对自己说：我很笨。

sentences.en: So, the first thing we thought about was, when bad events occur to you, Shankar, do you reflexively believe they're going to last forever?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们考虑的第一件事是：尚卡尔，当坏事发生在你身上时，你会下意识地认为它们会永远持续下去吗？

sentences.en: Or do you believe, no, just this one time?
sentences.zh: 还是你会认为：不，只是这一次而已？

sentences.en: The second dimension we worried about was pervasive versus local.
sentences.zh: 我们担心的第二个维度是普遍性与局限性。

sentences.en: And that is, you're rejected by your girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你被女朋友拒绝了。
你可能会认为：我不值得被爱。
嗯，“不值得被爱”是普遍性的。

sentences.en: And it means no matter who you come across, you're not going to find love.
sentences.zh: 这意味着无论你遇到谁，你都找不到真爱。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you might say, that's her.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你可能会说：那是她的问题。

sentences.en: And we postulated that people who believed that helplessness was pervasive would go on to generalize across situations.
sentences.zh: 我们推测，那些认为无助感是普遍性的人，往往会将其推广到各种情境中。

sentences.en: People who believed it was temporary would recover quickly.
sentences.zh: 而那些认为它是暂时性的人，则会很快恢复。

sentences.en: So, we began to look at the way people interpreted the bad events in their lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们开始观察人们解读生活中坏事的方式。

sentences.en: And this opened up an enormous literature on learned optimism.
sentences.zh: 这开启了关于“习得性乐观”的大量文献。

sentences.en: And it basically showed that the people who became helpless in the laboratory believed the helplessness was permanent, pervasive,
sentences.zh: 它基本上表明，在实验室中变得无助的人，认为这种无助是永久的、普遍的，
并且通常是他们自己的错。

sentences.en: The third of people who didn't become helpless believed it was temporary.
sentences.zh: 而那三分之一没有变得无助的人，认为这只是暂时的。

sentences.en: It was just this one situation.
sentences.zh: 这只是这一种情况而已。

sentences.en: So, having established the importance of explanatory styles, Marty,
sentences.zh: 那么，在确立了归因风格的重要性之后，马蒂，

sentences.en: you began to generate evidence that an optimistic or pessimistic explanatory style can significantly affect how people go about pursuing goals.
sentences.zh: 你开始产生证据表明，乐观或悲观的归因风格会显著影响人们追求目标的方式。

sentences.en: One place you explored this was at the West Point Military Academy.
sentences.zh: 你探索这一点的地方之一是西点军校。

sentences.en: Paint a picture for me of that study.
sentences.zh: 请为我描绘一下那项研究。

sentences.en: So, we not only asked the question about depression.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不仅提出了关于抑郁症的问题。

sentences.en: So, what we did was to take large groups of people at time one,
sentences.zh: 我们所做的是在第一阶段选取大量人群，

sentences.en: and then go on to predict who's going to become depressed.
sentences.zh: 然后去预测谁会变得抑郁。

sentences.en: And it turned out the pessimists, the people who believed it's me, it's going to last forever,
sentences.zh: 结果证明，悲观主义者，即那些认为“是我的错”、“它会永远持续下去”的人，

sentences.en: are between two and eight times as likely to become depressed.
sentences.zh: 变得抑郁的可能性是乐观者的两到八倍。

sentences.en: And so, we then asked the question, let's test this in the real world.
sentences.zh: 于是，我们提出了一个问题：让我们在现实世界中测试一下。

sentences.en: And so, one thing we did is we went to West Point.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们做的一件事就是去了西点军校。

sentences.en: And West Point at the time, and still does to some extent,
sentences.zh: 当时的西点军校，在某种程度上现在依然如此，
有一种叫做“野兽营”的训练。

sentences.en: Well, West Point is one of the most selective schools in the United States.
sentences.zh: 西点军校是美国录取标准最严格的学校之一。

sentences.en: These are very highly qualified young men and women.
sentences.zh: 这些都是非常优秀的年轻人。

sentences.en: But in the first six weeks, in mid-summer, in July,
sentences.zh: 但在最初的六周，在仲夏的七月，

sentences.en: and they're put through six weeks of helplessness experience,
sentences.zh: 并被投入到六周的无助感体验中，

sentences.en: in which the attempt is explicitly to break them.
sentences.zh: 其目的明确就是要击垮他们。

sentences.en: They're woken up at four in the morning,
And my memory is that about a third of the candidates drop out.
sentences.zh: 我的记忆中，大约有三分之一的候选人退出了。
所以，我们提出了一个问题：

sentences.en: could you predict from day one in Beast Barracks who was going to drop out?
sentences.zh: 你能从“野兽营”的第一天就预测出谁会退出吗？

sentences.en: And it turned out it was the pessimists who dropped out.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，退出的正是那些悲观主义者。

sentences.en: We then looked at something very similar about the grades you get in college.
sentences.zh: 我们随后观察了关于大学成绩的类似情况。

sentences.en: We looked at the optimists and the pessimists,
sentences.zh: 我们观察了乐观主义者和悲观主义者，

sentences.en: who does much better than their talent augers?
sentences.zh: 谁的表现远超他们的天赋预期？

sentences.en: I had been working on learned helplessness and optimism in Olympic swimming.
sentences.zh: 我当时正在研究奥运会游泳运动员的习得性无助和乐观精神。

sentences.en: And I had just come back from a day of looking at our Olympic swimming data.
sentences.zh: 我刚从查看奥运游泳数据的一天工作中回来。

sentences.en: and it was an insurance salesman.
And I hung up on him.
gee, this must be an awfully difficult job.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这一定是一份非常艰难的工作。

sentences.en: I mean, people hanging up on you all the time.
sentences.zh: 我是说，人们总是挂你的电话。

sentences.en: And it so happened that the month before,
I had become friendly from a professional meeting with the CEO of Metropolitan Life.
sentences.zh: 我在一次专业会议上与大都会人寿保险公司的首席执行官成为了朋友。

sentences.en: And I had told him about optimism and pessimism.
sentences.zh: 我曾向他讲述过乐观和悲观。

sentences.en: if you ever have an application to life insurance,
sentences.zh: 如果你有关于人寿保险的申请，

sentences.en: how do you hire a life insurance salesman?
sentences.zh: 你如何招聘人寿保险推销员？

sentences.en: there's an SAT of life insurance,
Do you want to make a lot of money?
And we hire 5,000 new salesmen a year because of this.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我们每年雇佣 5000 名新销售员。

sentences.en: They just can't take the rejection.
sentences.zh: 他们只是无法承受拒绝。

sentences.en: I think I've got a teSt.
sentences.zh: 我想我有一个测试方法。

sentences.en: That might predict who can stick with a difficult job like life insurance.
sentences.zh: 或许能预测出谁能坚持从事像人寿保险这样困难的工作。

sentences.en: We've just found out it predicts a grade point average,
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚发现它能预测平均绩点，

sentences.en: and it predicts Olympic swimming success.
sentences.zh: 也能预测奥运会游泳比赛的成功率。
也许它也能预测职业上的成功。

sentences.en: Metropolitan Life started to give the teSt.
sentences.zh: 大都会人寿保险公司开始使用这个测试。

sentences.en: they found that the pessimistic life insurance salesman is more optimistic than you or me.
sentences.zh: 他们发现悲观的人寿保险推销员比你我更乐观。

sentences.en: You have to be Frankensteinianly optimistic to even start.
sentences.zh: 你必须具备像弗兰肯斯坦那样疯狂的乐观精神，才能开始这项工作。

sentences.en: And then they hired a special force of 140 salespeople who knocked the top off of optimism scale.
sentences.zh: 随后，他们雇佣了一支由 140 名销售人员组成的特别部队，他们的乐观指数爆表。

sentences.en: This special force outsold everyone at MetLife.
sentences.zh: 这支特别部队的销售业绩超过了大都会人寿的所有人。

sentences.en: And by the end of four years,
75% as opposed to 10% were still working.
sentences.zh: 75% 的人仍在工作，而普通组只有 10%。

sentences.en: So we basically found across success in beast barracks,
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上发现，在军校训练、

sentences.en: and difficult jobs that the optimists did better than the pessimists.
sentences.zh: 以及困难的工作中，乐观者都比悲观者表现得更好。

sentences.en: And they were the people who didn't become helpless in the laboratory.
sentences.zh: 而且他们是在实验室里不会变得无助的那类人。

sentences.en: Most of us think our lives are shaped by events.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人认为生活是由事件塑造的。

sentences.en: But just as important is the meaning we assign to those events.
sentences.zh: 但同样重要的是我们赋予这些事件的意义。

sentences.en: The way we interpret a setback today
sentences.zh: 我们今天解读挫折的方式，

sentences.en: can quietly influence the decisions we make tomorrow
sentences.zh: 会悄然影响我们明天的决策，

sentences.en: and the future we ultimately create.
sentences.zh: 以及我们最终创造的未来。

sentences.en: we'll explore what are the most powerful forces in human psychology.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨人类心理中最强大的力量。

sentences.en: The belief that our choices can shape what happens next.
sentences.zh: 那就是相信我们的选择可以塑造接下来发生的事情。
您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。
我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.zh: 这段对话是否唤起了您自己感到无助的经历？

sentences.en: Or has it reminded you of a time when you stepped up
sentences.zh: 或者它是否让您想起曾经挺身而出，

sentences.en: and took charge of your own destiny?

sentences.zh: 或者关于乐观与悲观科学的问题或评论，

sentences.zh: 请找一个非常安静的房间，用手机录下一段语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Agency is the opposite of learned helplessness.

sentences.en: And that's the belief that in the here and now,
you can accomplish a specific goal.

sentences.en: So this idea of agency is something that fascinates you.
